quote.text: [8] Consider who it is that you praise when you praise people dispassionately: is it those who are just, or unjust?—‘Those who are just.’—The temperate or the intemperate?—‘The temperate.’—The self-controlled or the dissolute?—‘The self-controlled.’ [9] —You should know, then, that if you make yourself a person of that kind, you’ll be making yourself beautiful; but if you neglect these virtues, you’re bound to be ugly, whatever techniques you adopt to make yourself appear beautiful.
quote.author: Epictetus
quote.aiInsight:
• Parenthood: Emphasize teaching your children the value of inner virtues—justice, temperance, and self-control—so they may develop true beauty from within.
  • By leading through example in your daily interactions, you foster a household where integrity is celebrated over superficial appearances.
  • Leadership: As a leader, model the character you wish to see in others; prioritize ethical behavior and self-discipline to inspire trust and respect among your followers.
  • Remember that true leadership is not about projecting an image, but about embodying the virtues that earn genuine admiration and loyalty.
  • Product Management: Just as a product’s success stems from its inherent quality rather than mere aesthetics, so too does a team’s effectiveness depend on the virtuous qualities of its members.
  • Focus on developing a culture of responsibility and balanced judgment, ensuring that every decision reflects the inner values that drive long-term success and authenticity.
